scenes.heading: Warehouse SQL & Semi-Structured Data
scenes.narration: Modern warehouses speak rich analytical SQL and can query JSON directly without forcing it into rigid columns first.

scenes.heading: SQL beyond the basics
bullets: Window functions rank, run totals, and compare rows without self-joins.
Common table expressions break complex logic into readable steps.
Semi-structured types like VARIANT hold nested JSON natively.
Built-in functions flatten, cast, and navigate nested data on the fly.
scenes.narration: Analytical SQL adds window functions and CTEs that make complex queries both powerful and readable. Warehouses also store semi-structured data in flexible types like VARIANT. That means you can load JSON as-is and still query deep into its nested fields.

scenes.heading: Querying JSON in place
scenes.narration: You load raw JSON straight into a VARIANT column with no upfront schema. Path syntax lets you pull out individual fields, and a flatten operation expands nested arrays into rows. Finally you cast the values to proper types when you need clean, typed results.

scenes.heading: Extracting fields from JSON
scenes.code:
-- events.payload is a VARIANT holding JSON
SELECT
  payload:user_id::INT           AS user_id,
  payload:action::STRING         AS action,
  item.value:sku::STRING         AS sku
FROM events,
     LATERAL FLATTEN(input => payload:items) AS item
WHERE payload:action::STRING = 'purchase';
scenes.narration: Here the colon syntax reaches into the JSON payload to grab the user id and action, and the double colon casts them to real types. The LATERAL FLATTEN call expands the items array so each element becomes its own row. The result turns messy nested JSON into a clean tabular view ready for analysis.

scenes.text: Warehouse SQL combines advanced analytics with native JSON support, so you query flexible data without a rigid schema up front.
scenes.narration: You get advanced analytical SQL and native semi-structured support together, letting you explore flexible data without wrestling it into columns first.
